tagline: Over the Sierra Madre, past mining camps that came and went.
intro: Out of Encampment, WYO 70 climbs west into the little-visited Sierra Madre of the Medicine Bow National Forest and crosses the Continental Divide at Battle Pass, 9,955 feet up. On the far side it leaves the forest, dips for under a mile into Colorado at Slater, and runs down through Savery and Dixon to Baggs.
The pass is named for an 1841 fight between fur trappers and Native Americans. The mining came around 1900, and Battle is one of many ghost towns it left in the Sierra Madre.
season: Travel Wyoming says the aspen color at Aspen Alley, up Forest Road 801 to the north, generally peaks in late September.

moments.title: Encampment
moments.text: Around 1900 this was a copper town, fed by a sixteen-mile steam tramway from the mountains that was, at the time, the longest in the world.

moments.title: Battle
moments.text: Founded in 1898 as a resting stop on the wagon road to the Ferris-Haggarty mine, Battle was bypassed by the tramway in 1902 and was a ghost town by 1905.

moments.title: Battle Lake overlook
moments.text: Edison vacationed by the lake in 1878, and, so the story goes, a broken bamboo fishing pole glowing in his campfire gave him an idea for the light bulb filament.

practical: The highway over Battle Pass is closed in winter, from November to April.

sources.label: Travel Wyoming, Battle Pass Scenic Byway
